title: Provenance-driven tool-call eval harness for selection & arg validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated eval harness that ties tool/function-calling quality signals to exact model/config provenance so we can detect regressions introduced by model updates or runtime config changes. The harness will measure: (1) tool selection accuracy (did the model choose the correct tool given a prompt and tool catalog), (2) argument validation/completeness (are required args present, types/formats conform to the tool schema), and (3) downstream end-to-end success rate for a small set of canonical flows. Key differentiator: each run will snapshot the model version, quantization/profile, runtime flags, and routing policy to create an immutable provenance record for triage and automated bisection.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness runs on CI for every model/config change and produces a signed provenance blob.
2) Metrics emitted: tool_selection_accuracy, arg_schema_conformance, false_positive_rate (tool chosen when none needed), missed_tool_rate.
3) Each CI failure attaches failing examples and a minimized delta repro to the Linear ticket.
4) Dashboard tile with trend lines + alert when selection accuracy drops >5% relative to baseline over 24h.
5) Integration tests covering at least 10 canonical tool-calling prompts across 3 models/quant profiles.
progress_updates:
2026-02-18: spike complete — evaluated existing eval datasets and discovered coverage gaps around chained tool calls and optional arguments.
2026-02-24: PoC harness implemented that records model/config provenance and runs selection/arg checks locally. PoC repo: github.com/redwood-inference/toolcall-provenance (PR: #514).
2026-03-02: Added arg-schema conformance checker using JSON Schema derived from tool manifests; discovered a formatting mismatch bug in the RL prompt normalization step.
2026-03-10: Hooked harness into CI for runtime-2.3 branch; initial CI run flagged 2 regressions (one in argument serialization, one in tool selection on edge-case prompts). Investigating; creating minimized repros.
technical_notes:
- Provenance keys: model-id, model-hash, quant-profile, compiler-kernels-hash, runtime-flags, commit-sha.
- Selection scoring: top-k tool probability + heuristic tie-breaker using tool usage priors.
- Arg validation: JSON Schema + custom validators for file/uri types and auth tokens.
- Failure artifacts: canonical prompt, model logits snapshot for tool tokens, normalized args, and minimal diff between last good and current configs.
- Storage: artifacts uploaded to S3 with lifecycle 90d; provenance index in Postgres for fast lookups.
- Privacy: redact any customer PII from failing artifacts before attaching to tickets.
testing_plan:
1) Create goldset of 50 prompts across domains (search, calculators, booking, commerce).
2) Run harness daily on nightly model builds and on every PR touching runtime or model onboarding.
3) Inject synthetic regressions (simulated kernel switch, quant mismatch) to validate detection windows and alert thresholds.
4) Backfill 30 days of runs for the current model family to compute baseline metrics.
5) Run end-to-end replay for two customer-facing flows with QA sign-off before gating production rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: enable harness in CI for runtime-2.3 and collect baseline (2 weeks).
Phase 2: add dashboard and alerts; route failures to triage channel with automated minimized repro (1 week).
Phase 3: enforce gate on Dedicated and Private deploys: block merges when tool_selection_accuracy drops under threshold unless a rollback plan is documented.
Phase 4: integrate with rollout policies to auto-fallback to previous model variant on severe regressions.
open_questions:
- What is the exact threshold for automated rollback vs. notify-only for Trusted customers?
- Should we include token-level alignment checks (logit attribution) as part of the standard CI run or keep as on-demand deeper analysis?
- Team owning schema derivation for third-party tool manifests (internal vs. solutions eng).
